text:
elaine: Gateway Health just confirmed a short-term enterprise commit. Need a quick preflight: throughput profile, reserved GPU sizing, autoscale policy, and answers for the security questionnaire. Can infra + pricing sync at 15:00 PT? We have a legal deadline EOD tomorrow.

mike: copying traffic shape we got from their SRE: steady 250 rps, periodic daily spike to ~1k rps (10-15m), one weekly marketing surge that can hit ~5k rps for ~30m. avg tokens per request ~150. SLO: 99.9 p99 latency target for interactive chat.

nina: rough infra callout: for rdx-3b-quant (our recommended quantized variant) plan is: reserve 6 GPUs for the steady baseline, autoscale up to 18 for sustained 1k rps, and allow burst credits to reach 24 GPUs for the 5k short surge. Preheat window: 45m to warm KV cache and model weights for consistent tail latency. Canary: rollout at 10% of traffic during first 2 hours.

mike: can you lay out the math quickly so sales can quote? they want an explicit preheat duration and what happens if we hit bursts above reserved+credits.

nina: math quick note: baseline 250 rps ~6 GPUs (with batching/kv caching); 1k rps ~18 GPUs; 5k rps needs burst pool + spillover to cheaper model fallback if GPUs exhausted. If burst > credits, requests will queue at per-customer QoS with 30s soft timeout, then fallback to smaller model (rdx-1b) for degraded latency.

sridhar: pricing notes: reserved discount applies to monthly committed GPUs (we offer 20% off list on a 3mo commit). Burst credits billed at usage rate; recommend adding a small buffer line item for burst credit burn. Legal asked about cost overrun guardrails — propose alerting + automatic cap at 24 GPUs with notification to Gateway.

larry: on the security questionnaire: they asked for KMS/HSM details, SOC2 attestation date, data residency in us-west-2, VPC peering options, and audit log retention policy (they want 1 year). I can dump answers but need the ops diagram and the VPC peering playbook linked.

elaine: @larry please take the questionnaire, flag any gaps. @nina can you attach the autoscale config we'll propose?

nina: posting config snippet:
```yaml
autoscale:
  min: 6
  target_utilization: 65%
  max: 24
  "burst_policy": "burst_credits"
  preheat_window_minutes: 45
  canary_percent: 10
  "fallback_model": "rdx-1b-quant"
```

deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy for rdx-3b-quant at 2026-03-23T22:00:00Z (will route 10% traffic for 2h). :rocket:

mike: for the sales quote I'll need an explicit monthly estimate: reserved cost + expected burst credits (assume 6 surt months). sridhar can you draft a pricing line with two options: (A) conservative reserve 6 + buffer credits, (B) aggressive reserve 12 and lower burst burn.

sridhar: will do. Also adding preheat engineering support as a billed service (2x ops during first week) so we can guarantee KV warmup windows.

larry: assembling questionnaire answers now. Need a quick diagram of VPC peering and KMS flow from infra — @nina can you point to the repo or paste a small diagram?

nina: repo link: https://git.redwood.internal/infra/gateway-health-onboarding (private). I'll paste minimal ascii diagram in the doc.

elaine: awesome — meeting 15:00 PT confirmed. I'll send invite and attach this thread to the ticket. Thanks all — try to keep answers tight (legal is strict). :thumbsup:

mike: noted. I'll prep the traffic-runway appendix so their SREs can simulate the surge.

elaine: final ask: if we need a fallback routing policy for >=10% dropped requests, prefer immediate model fallback vs queueing? Gateway prefers degraded but immediate responses. We'll default to fallback model and note latency/quality tradeoffs in the quote.

nina: agreed — fallback model route is default for this customer during overrun. I'll add quality-monitor hooks and an eval runbook.

elaine: thanks — last_message_ts updated.
